image_description: A high-angle shot of a group of six hamsters huddled together on wood shavings and pink paper bedding. The subjects include a large golden/tan adult, a calico-patterned adult, and four smaller pups with black-and-white or grey-and-white markings. They are arranged in a pile, with some overlapping.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Broad head with prominent cheek pouches extending to shoulders.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the general head shape is round, the specific anatomical feature of 'prominent cheek pouches' is not visually distinct or bulging in any of the subjects. The faces appear smooth without the characteristic distension associated with full cheek pouches.
Visible eyes on the golden hamster and the calico hamster are small, dark, and bead-like, consistent with the taxonomy.
Ears are visible on the upper subjects; they are rounded and proportionally large relative to the head size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Stocky compact body with diminutive, rounded proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All subjects exhibit the characteristic stout, oval-shaped body plan of hamsters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dense short fur in golden, brown, black, or white coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Fur texture appears dense and short. Colorations match the allowed palette (golden, agouti, black, white).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short legs with clawed digits; hind feet slightly elongated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Legs are largely tucked under the bodies or occluded by other hamsters. Digits and claws are not resolvable at this resolution/angle.
Tails are completely occluded by the huddling posture and body overlap.

artifact_observations.location: Interface between the top calico hamster and the middle golden hamster
artifact_observations.reasoning: The boundary where the two animals touch lacks clear separation. Fur textures seem to bleed into one another, creating a 'melted' connection rather than two distinct physical objects resting against each other.

The anatomy of this subject is distorted. The rear half of the body tapers unnaturally and seems to lack defined hind legs, appearing more like a slug or larva than a rodent. The transition from body to tail/rear is structurally ambiguous.

The background texture has a repetitive, smudged quality typical of AI generation, lacking the crisp, individual detail of real wood chips. Some shavings appear to merge with the hamster fur at the edges.

To detect fusion artifacts and edge bleeding between the overlapping animals.
